report.incidentSummary: On 2026-10-07 at 11:55 IST (06:25 UTC), the Assistant on-call team reported INC-5200 (SEV2): assistant replies taking 20+ seconds and some conversations failing with 'Something went wrong' since approximately 11:20 IST (05:50 UTC). The team suspected the knowledge index rebuild initiated at 11:00 IST (05:30 UTC). Investigation revealed that the knowledge index remained healthy and was not the cause. Instead, beginning at 05:50 UTC, the external LLM provider began returning HTTP 429 'Too Many Requests (quota exceeded: tokens per minute, limit=200000)'. Because steady-state assistant traffic consumed 220,000-267,000 TPM, requests were rate-limited. Assistant-orchestrator's retry backoffs stretched request duration to 20-26 seconds, and conversations that exhausted all 3 attempts failed with fallback generic error messages (~6% error rate).
report.rootCauseStatement: The incident was caused by external rate limiting from llm-provider: starting at 2026-10-07T05:50:00Z (11:20 IST), llm-provider enforced an account tokens-per-minute quota of 200,000 TPM. Because normal assistant traffic runs between 210,000 and 267,000 TPM, calls were rejected with HTTP 429 ('quota exceeded: tokens per minute, limit=200000'). Configured retries with exponential backoff on assistant-orchestrator stretched conversation response times to 20-26 seconds, and conversations that exhausted 3 attempts failed with generic fallback messages. The knowledge index rebuild initiated at 05:30 UTC was coincidental and was ruled out as a cause.

hypotheses.cause: External LLM provider enforced or reduced the tokens-per-minute quota to 200,000 TPM, causing widespread HTTP 429 rate limiting on steady-state traffic of ~220,000-267,000 TPM. Retry loops added 20+ seconds of latency and caused fallback errors after 3 failed attempts.
hypotheses.rationale: Direct log and metric evidence shows HTTP 429 quota errors starting exactly at 05:50 UTC with limit=200,000. Prior steady-state token rate was 220k-267k tokens/min. Retries (2 retries, 3 attempts total) with exponential backoffs accounted directly for the 20-26s conversation response times and 6% fallback failure rate.

hypotheses.cause: Knowledge-index rebuild (CHG-48222) saturated retrieval serving nodes, causing assistant-orchestrator to wait on document search.
hypotheses.rationale: Ruled out: The rebuild started at 05:30 UTC, whereas symptoms began 20 minutes later at 05:50 UTC. Knowledge-index p95 search latency peaked at 369 ms (well within the 800 ms timeout), search error rate remained 0.10%, and assistant delays persisted at 24+ seconds after the rebuild completed at 07:10 UTC.
Ruled out: The last assistant-orchestrator release (version 0.42.1, CHG-48496) occurred on 2026-10-06 at 12:26 UTC, nearly 17 hours before incident onset.

facts.statement: An infrastructure change (CHG-48222) initiated a full index rebuild on knowledge-index at 2026-10-07T05:30:00.000Z.

assistant-orchestrator latency_p95_ms increased from ~6,200 ms to 12,765 ms at 05:50 UTC and stayed between 23,000 ms and 25,500 ms through 07:25 UTC; llm_latency_p95_ms jumped from ~5,100 ms to ~22,500 ms at the same time.
knowledge-index latency_p95_ms rose from ~85 ms to a peak of 369.3 ms during the rebuild (between 05:30 UTC and 07:10 UTC), while its error rate stayed constant at ~0.10%.
The knowledge-index rebuild completed around 07:10 UTC, with docs_ingested_per_min dropping from over 200/min to ~4/min by 07:15 UTC.
assistant-orchestrator rate_limited_count surged from 0 to 33.38/min at 05:50 UTC and ~60-79/min thereafter; retry_count surged from ~0.5/min to ~50-65/min.
assistant-orchestrator consumed between 211,000 and 267,000 tokens per minute prior to 05:50 UTC without triggering rate limits.

At 05:50:04 UTC, assistant-orchestrator began receiving HTTP 429 Too Many Requests errors from llm-provider stating 'quota exceeded: tokens per minute, limit=200000' and retrying after backoffs of 2 to 8 seconds.
Conversations that failed all 3 retry attempts logged an ERROR stating 'failed: llm-provider 429 after 3 attempts; returned fallback message' and returned the generic fallback message to users.
assistant-orchestrator error_rate rose from ~0.5% before 05:50 UTC to ~6.0% after 05:50 UTC.
compliance-filter and user-context-service maintained normal p95 latencies (~108 ms and ~175 ms respectively) and low error rates throughout the incident window.

inferences.statement: The 20+ second response time is directly caused by assistant-orchestrator executing up to two retries with exponential backoff against llm-provider's 429 rate limit responses.
The 'Something went wrong' errors reported by users represent conversations where all 3 LLM attempts were rejected with HTTP 429, triggering assistant-orchestrator's fallback response.
The knowledge index rebuild was a red herring: retrieval latency peaked at ~369 ms (well below the 800 ms timeout), and assistant degradation continued past 07:10 UTC when the rebuild finished.

assumptions.statement: The LLM provider either reduced our account's token-per-minute quota to 200,000 TPM at 05:50 UTC or enforced an existing threshold that was previously unenforced or shared with another pool.

timeline.event: Full index rebuild build-4121 initiated on knowledge-index (CHG-48222).
knowledge-index latency_p95_ms rises from ~85 ms to ~350 ms as build 4121 warms, but remains well below 800 ms timeout.
llm-provider begins returning HTTP 429 Too Many Requests (quota exceeded: tokens per minute, limit=200000) on assistant-orchestrator outbound calls.
assistant-orchestrator latency_p95_ms jumps to 12.7s and then 24.1s; retry_count and rate_limited_count spike to ~60-70/min.
First logged fallback failure returned to user after 3 failed 429 attempts (conversation c_60473f6b).
Assistant on-call team reports INC-5200 (SEV2).
knowledge-index rebuild build-4121 completes; ingestion rate returns to ~4 docs/min and search latency recovers to ~85 ms.
assistant-orchestrator latency remains degraded at ~24.5s and rate_limited_count remains elevated at ~73/min, confirming independence from knowledge-index rebuild.

confidence.rationale: Evidence directly demonstrates that llm-provider returned HTTP 429 with 'quota exceeded: tokens per minute, limit=200000' beginning precisely at 05:50 UTC, causing assistant-orchestrator's retry count and LLM latency to spike to 20+ seconds. Knowledge-index rebuild was definitively ruled out by latency metrics well below configured timeouts and persistence of symptoms after rebuild completion.

gaps.description: External account administration logs or billing/quota notifications from llm-provider are not directly observable within internal service logs.
gaps.impact: Cannot distinguish whether the provider lowered the quota via account change or began enforcing an existing 200,000 TPM limit at 05:50 UTC.

recommendedActions.action: Contact llm-provider support or upgrade the tier/quota to increase the tokens-per-minute (TPM) limit to at least 350,000 TPM to comfortably accommodate peak traffic.
recommendedActions.rationale: Our normal baseline traffic consumes 220,000 to 267,000 tokens/min, which exceeds the newly enforced 200,000 TPM ceiling.
recommendedActions.verification: Verify via assistant-orchestrator metrics that rate_limited_count drops to zero and 429 warnings cease in logs.

recommendedActions.action: Implement request-level token budgeting or concurrency throttling in assistant-orchestrator to smooth token spikes and avoid bursty 429 rejections.
recommendedActions.rationale: Proactive client-side rate limiting prevents hitting provider hard limits and cascading retry storms.
recommendedActions.verification: Check that assistant-orchestrator retry_count and latency_p95_ms remain stable under load.

recommendedActions.action: Add alerting for llm-provider rate_limited_count > 5/min on assistant-orchestrator.
recommendedActions.rationale: The team was alerted on assistant latency after 35 minutes; direct alerting on rate_limited_count will detect quota constraints immediately.
recommendedActions.verification: Simulate rate limit alerts in staging or check alert rule registration in monitoring configuration.

## Inferences
- The 20+ second response time is directly caused by assistant-orchestrator executing up to two retries with exponential backoff against llm-provider's 429 rate limit responses. [ev_3, ev_4, ev_10, ev_16]
- The 'Something went wrong' errors reported by users represent conversations where all 3 LLM attempts were rejected with HTTP 429, triggering assistant-orchestrator's fallback response. [ev_6, ev_10, ev_16]
- The knowledge index rebuild was a red herring: retrieval latency peaked at ~369 ms (well below the 800 ms timeout), and assistant degradation continued past 07:10 UTC when the rebuild finished. [ev_3, ev_5, ev_14, ev_19]

## Assumptions
- The LLM provider either reduced our account's token-per-minute quota to 200,000 TPM at 05:50 UTC or enforced an existing threshold that was previously unenforced or shared with another pool.
